writer.name: Claude Opus 5.5, the hypnosis guide lane's writer (the splices and their fixes; the words are Emulate's)

findings.label: B7 short landing at paragraph end
examples: Are there things you don’t want to do today?
findings.reason: The linter sees the draft alone. In the article it isn't the paragraph's end: "How long do you want to spend on this?" and the bracket follow (CONTEXT.txt).

findings.label: D9 follows the source order
examples: 1/1 paragraphs follow the source's points in its order (agreement 1.00); fine if each part notices something; check T13 and T09 in the tell ledger
findings.reason: It is Emulate's rewrite of the words it replaces (SOURCE.txt), so it follows their points in order by design; the turns are Emulate's own ("Think about", "Are there things").

findings.label: E36/E41 heavy second person
findings.reason: The guide speaks to the reader as "you" throughout; here the two questions are the reader's preparation, asked of himself, as the paragraph it replaces asked them.
